phases.objective: Restore registration of the canonical CI workflow and make its pull-request surface read-only by retiring the completed PR #3945 one-shot Production closure from the permanent workflow.

e2e_journeys.actor: GitHub Actions workflow registrar and pull-request runner
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A same-repository pull request targets main after the unavailable runner context and completed one-shot mutation job are removed from ci.yml.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: GitHub materializes the workflow named CI, its four permanent validation jobs remain available, and the pull-request workflow contains no repository-write permission, runtime mutation secret, or historical Production closure path.
steps: Read the canonical CI workflow and verify its name and main/Production pull-request trigger.
Verify the syntax, unit and integration, execution resolver, and architecture drift jobs remain registered.
Reject the historical local-connector-production-closure job from the permanent workflow.
Reject issue-write and pull-request-write permissions from canonical pull-request CI.
Reject the historical BACKEND_API_KEY binding, closure script invocation, and one-shot PR #3945 token.
Observe creation of both CI and CI Pull Request Recovery on the exact pull-request head and execute the complete E2E and registration regression checks.
assertions: The canonical workflow remains named CI and continues targeting main and Production pull requests.
All four permanent CI validation jobs remain present.
The completed PR #3945 one-shot Production closure is absent from canonical CI.
The workflow contains no issue-write or pull-request-write permission and no runtime mutation secret.
No trigger broadening, deployment, Hostinger/provider mutation, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, protected-ref mutation, or external business send is introduced.

phases.objective: Verify canonical CI registration across opened, synchronize, and ready-for-review pull-request events.
Reject future unavailable workflow contexts and embedded pull-request mutation jobs before they suppress or invalidate CI registration.
Prove Draft and Ready exact-head cycles with both canonical CI and CI Pull Request Recovery visible.
Retire the temporary recovery workflow only after canonical CI registration remains stable across governed pull requests.
